items.title: L^2 kernel operators and Hilbert-Schmidt operators on R^3

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.3 pp. 139-145 (Hilbert-Schmidt operators defined as integral operators with L^2 kernels)
Theo Buehler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis (ETH lecture notes, 2017), Section 5.2.3 pp. 224-227 (the spectrum of a compact operator; finite-rank and norm-limit structure)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of Lebesgue
(equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and write $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
for the same construction over the product with Lebesgue measure; identify
Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^6$ with the completion of the product of
Lebesgue measures on the two $\mathbb R^3$ factors.

**Kernel data and sections.** Let $k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, an almost-everywhere equivalence class, and choose a finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable representative $k_0:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C$. When $f\in L^2$ is used, choose likewise a finite-valued Lebesgue-measurable representative $f_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C$. For almost every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, the section $k_x(y):=k_0(x,y)$ is measurable, by applying the completed-product Fubini theorem to the positive and negative parts of the real and imaginary components of $k_0$ ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]).

**Domain and action.** For $f\in L^2$ say that the integral defining $T_kf$
*exists at* $x\in\mathbb R^3$ if the section product
$y\mapsto k_0(x,y)f_0(y)$ is measurable and lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, and at such points put
$$(T_kf)(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}k_0(x,y)f_0(y)\,dy .$$
Define
$$D(T_k):=\Bigl\{f\in L^2:\ x\mapsto(T_kf)(x)\ \text{exists for almost every }x\text{ and agrees a.e. with a class in }L^2\Bigr\},$$
and for $f\in D(T_k)$ let $T_kf$ denote that class. The assignment
$f\mapsto T_kf$ is called the *$L^2$-kernel operator with kernel $k$*.

This definition is independent of both representative choices. If $k_1$ is
another representative of $k$, its disagreement set with $k_0$ is null for the
completed product Lebesgue measure. Fubini applied to the indicator of that
set gives $k_0(x,\cdot)=k_1(x,\cdot)$ almost everywhere for almost every
$x$. For each such $x$ and any representative of $f$, the two section products
therefore have the same $L^1$ status and, when integrable, the same integral.
Replacing $f_0$ by another representative changes the section product only on
a null set of $y$, so it too preserves integrability and the integral.
Consequently the almost-everywhere sections, the subset $D(T_k)\subseteq L^2$,
and the resulting output class are unchanged by either representative choice.

**Hilbert-Schmidt operators.** A linear operator $T$ on $L^2$ is called a
*Hilbert-Schmidt operator* if there is
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with $D(T)=D(T_k)$ and
$T=T_k$; such a $k$ is called an *$L^2$ kernel* of $T$.

This definition asserts nothing about whether $D(T_k)$ is all of $L^2$,
whether $T_k$ is bounded, or whether $T_k$ is compact; those properties are
proved in [[lem-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators-bounded-and-compact]]. A
finite product kernel $\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ with
$f_i,g_i\in L^2$ is also a class in $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$,
as the same lemma records, so $T_k$ is defined for it whenever that membership
is used.

items.title: L^2 kernel operators are bounded and compact

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.3 pp. 139-145 (an integral operator with L^2 kernel is bounded with norm at most the L^2 norm of its kernel and is compact)
Theo Buehler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis (ETH lecture notes, 2017), Section 5.2.3 pp. 224-227 (finite-rank operators are compact; norm limits of compact operators are compact)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and let
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with $T_k$ the
$L^2$-kernel operator of [[def-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators]]. Then:

(a) $D(T_k)=L^2$; $T_k$ is linear and bounded with
$\|T_kf\|_2\le\|k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\|f\|_2$ for every
$f\in L^2$, so $\|T_k\|\le\|k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}$;

(b) if $n\ge1$, $f_1,\dots,f_n,g_1,\dots,g_n\in L^2$ and
$k(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ a.e., then $k$ is a class in
$L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, the range of $T_k$ is contained
in $\operatorname{span}\{f_1,\dots,f_n\}$, and $T_k$ is compact;

(c) $T_k$ is compact; and

(d) for every sequence $(k_m)$ in
$L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with
$\|k_m-k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\to0$ one has
$T_{k_m}-T_k=T_{k_m-k}$ and
$\|T_{k_m}-T_k\|\le\|k_m-k\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3)}\to0$; in
particular $T_k$ is the operator-norm limit of finite-rank kernel operators.

No statement is made about the spectrum of $T_k$, about its singular values,
or about $L^2$ kernels of a given compact operator.

items.title: Closed semibounded symmetric forms and their associated operators

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.3 pp. 67-73 (quadratic forms, closedness, semiboundedness and the form domain of a self-adjoint operator)
Theo Buehler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis (ETH lecture notes, 2017), Chapter 6 pp. 305-333 (unbounded operators on Hilbert spaces: domains, adjoints and graphs)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V)$ and $(H,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_H)$ be
complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $i:V\to H$ be a linear map with dense
image.

**Symmetric forms.** A *sesquilinear form on $V$* is a map
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb C$ that is linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second; it is *symmetric* if
$a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$ for all $u,v\in V$, in which case $a(u,u)\in\mathbb R$
and $\operatorname{Re}a(u,v)=\operatorname{Re}\overline{a(v,u)}$.

**Bounded and semibounded.** Such a form is *bounded* if there is $C>0$ with
$|a(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ for all $u,v\in V$, and *semibounded below with
bound $M\ge0$* if $a(u,u)\ge-M\|i(u)\|_H^2$ for every $u\in V$.

**Form seminorm and closedness.** Let $M\ge0$ be a bound as above and define the
*form seminorm*
$$\|u\|_{a,M}:=\Bigl(\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+(M+1)\|i(u)\|_H^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\qquad(u\in V).$$
It is a seminorm because $a(u,v)+(M+1)\langle i(u),i(v)\rangle_H$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form; its Cauchy–Schwarz inequality follows by expanding its value on $u+tv$ and minimizing over the scalar $t$, and gives the triangle inequality. It need not separate points for a general dense-image map $i$. The form $a$ is *closed* if there are such an $M$ and constants $c,C>0$ with
$c\|u\|_V\le\|u\|_{a,M}\le C\|u\|_V$ for every $u\in V$; then
the form seminorm is a norm, and $(V,\|\cdot\|_{a,M})$ is complete because $V$ is. If $i$ is injective, it is already a norm before closedness, since its square is at least $\|i(u)\|_H^2$.

**Associated operator.** With $a$ and $i$ as above, define
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{u\in V:\ \text{there is }f\in H\text{ with }a(u,v)=\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H\text{ for every }v\in V\Bigr\},\qquad Au:=f .$$
The element $f$ is unique when it exists, because two candidates differ by an
element of $H$ orthogonal to the dense subspace $i(V)$, hence coincide;
$A$ is called the *operator associated with $a$*. This definition asserts
neither that $A$ is densely defined, nor that $A$ is symmetric, nor that $A$ is
self-adjoint or bounded below; the specific closed semibounded form of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] establishes those
properties for its own associated operator by a direct computation. When $V$
is a subspace of $H$ and $i$ is the inclusion, $\|i(u)\|_H$ is written
$\|u\|_H$ and the pairing $\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H$ is written
$\langle f,v\rangle$.

items.title: Three-dimensional Hardy bound

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations (Springer Universitext 2011), Comments on Chapter 8, p. 233 (the one-dimensional Hardy inequality on W^{1,p}_0(0,1) with the sharp constant p/(p-1)) and Comments on Chapter 9, p. 313 (Hardy's inequality ||u/d||_p <= C||Du||_p on bounded C^1 domains)

Wikipedia, 'Hardy's inequality' (encyclopedia article; secondary reference for the sharp multidimensional form: the L^p(R^n) norm of f/|x| is at most p/(n-p) times the L^p norm of the gradient, 1 <= p < n; the case n=3, p=2 gives the constant 2, whose square 4 is the constant of this lemma)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] with the weak gradient $\nabla u$ of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], write
$r(x):=|x|$, and write $\|u\|_2^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(x)|^2\,dx$ for the
$L^2$ norm of [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Then:

(a) for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\};\mathbb C)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{|u(x)|^2}{|x|^2}\,dx\le 4\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla u(x)|^2\,dx;$$

(b) the same inequality holds for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$;

(c) for every $u\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ the a.e.-defined function $x\mapsto u(x)/|x|$ lies in $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and satisfies $\|u/|\cdot|\|_2\le 2\|\nabla u\|_2$.

No constant smaller than $4$ is claimed, and no statement is made about
$\|u/|\cdot|\|_2$ for $u$ outside $W^{1,2}$.

items.title: Coulomb infinitesimal kinetic bound

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorem 6.4 p. 135 (Kato-Rellich) and Section 10.1 pp. 221-222 (Theorem 10.2: the Coulomb potential is relatively compact, hence infinitesimally bounded, with respect to -Laplacian; H^{(1)} is self-adjoint on H^2)

Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations (Springer Universitext 2011), Section 9.3 pp. 278-287 (Sobolev inequalities) and Comments on Chapter 9, p. 313 (Hardy's inequality, the model singular-potential estimate)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and let
$H_0:=-\Delta$ be the free operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
with domain $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]): $H_0=\mathcal F_2^*M_{4\pi^2|\xi|^2}\mathcal F_2$
and $H_0u=-\Delta u$ for $u\in D(H_0)$, where $\Delta u$ is the distributional
Laplacian. Write $M$ for the multiplication operator
$$M u:=\frac{u}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(M):=\Bigl\{u\in H:\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\in H\Bigr\},$$
and write $\|u\|_2=\|u\|_H$. Then:

(a) for every $u\in D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ one has $u/|\cdot|\in L^2$ and

$$\Bigl\|\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\Bigr\|_2\le 2\sqrt{\|u\|_2\,\|\Delta u\|_2}\,,\qquad \Bigl\|\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\Bigr\|_2\le \eta\|\Delta u\|_2+\frac1\eta\|u\|_2\quad(\eta>0);$$

(b) $M$ is a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with $D(H_0)\subseteq D(M)$, symmetric on $D(H_0)$, with $H_0$-bound zero in the sense that for every $\eta>0$ the pair $(\eta,\eta^{-1})$ is admissible for $M$ relative to $H_0$;

(c) for every $\gamma>0$ the operator
$$C:=H_0-\gamma M,\qquad D(C):=D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),$$
is self-adjoint on $H$, bounded below, and acts by $Cu=-\Delta u-\gamma u/|\cdot|$ for every $u\in D(C)$; for every $\eta\in(0,1/\gamma)$ one has $C\ge-\gamma\eta^{-1}/(1-\gamma\eta)$ in the quadratic-form sense.

No sharp lower bound of $C$ is claimed here, and no physical interpretation of
$C$, $H_0$, $\gamma$ or $\Delta$ is asserted.

items.title: Coulomb relative compactness

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.4 pp. 145-149 (relatively compact operators, the discrete and essential spectrum (6.27)-(6.28), and Weyl's theorem) and Section 10.1 pp. 221-222 (Theorem 10.2: V in L^infinity_infinity + L^2 is relatively compact with respect to H_0)

Theo Buehler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis (ETH lecture notes, 2017), Section 5.2.3 pp. 224-227 (the spectrum of a compact operator) and Section 5.3.4 pp. 243-246 (the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H_0=-\Delta$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
let $M u=u/|\cdot|$ be the multiplier of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with $D(M)\supseteq D(H_0)$,
and let $V:=-\gamma M$, so that $Vf=-\gamma f/|\cdot|$. For $z\notin\mathbb R$
write $R_0(z):=(H_0-z)^{-1}$
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[thm-self-adjoint-resolvent-estimate]]). Then:

(a) for every $z\notin\mathbb R$ there holds $R_0(z)=\mathcal F_2^*M_{m_z}\mathcal F_2$ with $m_z(\xi):=(4\pi^2|\xi|^2-z)^{-1}\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and $\|R_0(z)f\|_\infty\le\|m_z\|_2\|f\|_2$ for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(b) for every $z\notin\mathbb R$ there is $g_z\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with $R_0(z)f=g_z*f$ for every $f\in L^2$;

(c) for every bounded measurable $\chi$ with compact support the operator $M_\chi R_0(z)$ is Hilbert–Schmidt, hence compact;

(d) $V$ is $H_0$-compact ([[def-relative-compactness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]): $V$ is graph-norm bounded with respect to $H_0$ and $VR_0(z)$ is a compact operator for one, equivalently every, $z\notin\mathbb R$; explicitly $VR_0(z)=-\gamma M R_0(z)$ is compact.

No statement is made about compactness of $M$ itself, about point spectrum or
about any other spectral property of $H_0+V$; no physical interpretation is
asserted.

items.title: Coulomb essential spectrum

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 6.4 pp. 145-149 (Weyl's theorem: invariance of the essential spectrum under relatively compact perturbations) and Section 10.1 pp. 221-222 (sigma_ess(-Laplacian - gamma/|x|) = [0,infinity))

Theo Buehler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis (ETH lecture notes, 2017), Chapter 5 pp. 209-246 (spectral theory of bounded operators; compact and self-adjoint operators) and Chapter 6 pp. 305-333 (the spectrum of unbounded operators on Hilbert spaces)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$H_0=-\Delta$ with $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the free operator
of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
let $M$ be the multiplier $Mu=u/|\cdot|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]], and let
$$C:=H_0-\gamma M,\qquad D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),$$
be the self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c).
Write $\sigma_{\mathrm d}$, $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}$, $E$ for the discrete
spectrum, essential spectrum and spectral projection valued measure of
[[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]] and
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. Then:

(a) $C$ is bounded below and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,+\infty)$;

(b) every point of $\sigma(C)\cap(-\infty,0)$ lies in $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(C)$: it is an eigenvalue of $C$ of finite multiplicity isolated in $\mathbb R$, and the set of such eigenvalues is at most countable;

(c) the negative spectral subspace $E((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ is the closed linear span of the eigenspaces of $C$ for its negative eigenvalues.

No claim is made about the multiplicity or the number of the negative
eigenvalues, about the nonnegative part of the spectrum beyond
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C)=[0,\infty)$, or about any physical interpretation.

items.title: Angular radial unitary reduction

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.2 pp. 222-225 (spherical coordinates (10.16)-(10.21) and separation of the Coulomb eigenvalue equation) and Section 10.3 pp. 225-229 (Theorems 10.6-10.7: associated Legendre functions and the spherical harmonics Y_l^m as an orthonormal basis)

S. Axler, P. Bourdon, W. Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd edition, author-hosted full text, Chapter 5 'Harmonic Polynomials' pp. 73-105, in particular 'Spherical Harmonic Decomposition of L^2(S)' p. 78 and 'Explicit Bases of H_m(R^n) and H_m(S)' p. 92

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$, let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), and let
$(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
$L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]. Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with Lebesgue measure and inner product linear
in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$K:=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr;\mathbb C\bigr)$$
be the Hilbert direct sum over $l\ge0$, $-l\le m\le l$. For $\psi\in L^2$ and
each $(l,m)$ define the coefficient function and the reduced function
$$c_{lm}(r):=\int_{S^2}\psi(r\Omega)\overline{Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\quad(r>0,\ \text{a.e.}),\qquad u_{lm}(r):=r\,c_{lm}(r).$$
Then:

(a) for every $\psi\in L^2$ and every $(l,m)$ the function $u_{lm}$ is a well-defined element of $L^2((0,\infty),dr)$ depending only on the class of $\psi$, and $U\psi:=(u_{lm})_{l,m}$ is a linear isometry of $L^2$ into (indeed onto) $K$ with
$$\|U\psi\|_K^2=\sum_{l\ge0}\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\int_0^\infty|u_{lm}(r)|^2\,dr=\|\psi\|_{L^2}^2;$$

(b) $U$ is unitary, and for every $(u_{lm})\in K$ the finite-subset sums $\sum_{l\le N,\,|m|\le l}u_{lm}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ converge in $L^2$ to a function $\psi$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$;

(c) on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ every $f\in C^2$ satisfies, in the notation $\partial_r f$, $\Delta_{S^2}f$ of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]],
$$\Delta f=\partial_r^2f+\frac2r\partial_rf+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2}f;$$

(d) for every $l\ge0$, $m$, and $u\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$, the function $\psi:=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\subseteq H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, its image under $U$ is the finite-support vector with $(l,m)$-entry $u$, and
$$-\Delta\psi=\frac1r\Bigl(-u''(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\Bigr)Y_{lm}(\Omega),\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla\psi|^2\,dx=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr .$$

All statements are purely mathematical assertions about $L^2$ spaces, the
surface measure and the Laplacian; no physical interpretation and no statement
about operators with unbounded potentials is included.

items.title: Transported radial endpoint realization

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 9.1 pp. 181-186 (Sturm-Liouville operators, boundary conditions and self-adjoint realisations) and Section 10.4 p. 230 (Theorem 10.8: domain and essential spectrum of the radial Coulomb operator A_l)

Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations (Springer Universitext 2011), Section 8.6 pp. 231-233 (eigenfunction expansions and the variational characterisation of one-dimensional eigenvalues) and Section 9.5 pp. 291-298 (variational formulation of boundary value problems)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, let
$C:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c) when $\gamma>0$, and the free Fourier multiplier when $\gamma=0$,
and let $U$ be the unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] from $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$
onto $K=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2\bigl((0,\infty),dr\bigr)$, with coefficients
$u_{lm}=r\,c_{lm}$. For $l\ge0$ let $V_l$ be the closure of
$C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$ in $L^2(0,\infty;\mathbb C)$ for the norm
$$\|u\|_{V_l}^2:=\int_0^\infty\Bigl(\Bigl|u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr|^2+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}|u(r)|^2+|u(r)|^2\Bigr)dr,$$
realized as the space of $u\in L^2$ with $u'-\frac ur\in L^2$ and
$\int|u|^2/r^2<\infty$ in the distributional sense
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and define
$$a_l(u,v):=\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\overline{\Bigl(v'(r)-\frac{v(r)}{r}\Bigr)}\Bigl(u'(r)-\frac{u(r)}{r}\Bigr)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^2}u(r)\overline{v(r)}-\frac{\gamma}{r}u(r)\overline{v(r)}\Bigr]dr .$$
Then:

(a) $V_l$ is a dense linear subspace of $L^2(0,\infty)$ that is a Hilbert space for $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$, the inclusion $V_l\hookrightarrow L^2(0,\infty)$ is continuous, and $a_l$ is a bounded symmetric sesquilinear form on $V_l$ that is closed and semibounded below;

(b) the operator $A_l$ defined by
$$D(A_l):=\Bigl\{u\in V_l:\exists\,f\in L^2(0,\infty)\ \text{with}\ a_l(u,v)=\langle f,v\rangle\ \forall v\in V_l\Bigr\},\qquad A_lu:=f,$$
is well defined, self-adjoint and bounded below; $D(A_l)$ is dense in $V_l$ in the norm $\|\cdot\|_{V_l}$ and $a_l(u,u)=\langle A_lu,u\rangle$ for $u\in D(A_l)$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_l)$ the distributional identity $-u''+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)u=A_lu$ holds on $(0,\infty)$; consequently $u\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty)$, $u$ is of class $C^1$ with $u'$ locally absolutely continuous, and the identity holds pointwise almost everywhere on $(0,\infty)$; if moreover $A_lu=Eu$ for some constant $E\in\mathbb C$ (in particular if $u$ is an eigenfunction of $A_l$), then $u$ is of class $C^2$ on $(0,\infty)$ and the differential equation holds pointwise there;

(d) *block identity.* For $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with $U\psi=(u_{lm})$ one has $\psi\in D(C)$ if and only if $u_{lm}\in D(A_l)$ for every $(l,m)$ and $\sum_{l,m}\bigl(\|u_{lm}\|^2+\|A_lu_{lm}\|^2\bigr)<\infty$; then $U(C\psi)=(A_lu_{lm})_{l,m}$. Equivalently $UCU^*=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_l$ on $K$;

(e) *eigenfunction transport.* If $u\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu=Eu$ for some $E\in\mathbb R$, then the function $\psi(x):=u(r)Y_{l0}(\Omega)/r$ (with $x=r\Omega$) lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, satisfies $C\psi=E\psi$, and $r\mapsto u(r)/r$ is bounded on $(0,1]$; moreover $\psi$ is bounded and continuous on $\mathbb R^3$.

No endpoint boundary condition is imposed by hand: the domain $D(A_l)$ is the
form-domain realization transported from $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and no
physical interpretation of $A_l$, $C$, $U$ or $\gamma$ is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$,
$k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write
$$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$
and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let
$$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$
be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then:

(a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$;

(b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and
$$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$
is a $C^\infty$ solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ with $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$; it is, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, the only solution with $u(r)/r^{l+1}$ bounded as $r\downarrow0$; every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $c_1u_{\mathrm{reg}}+c_2u_2$ with $u_2$ defined near zero by $u_2(r):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)\int_{r_*}^r u_{\mathrm{reg}}(s)^{-2}ds$, where $0<r_*<\delta$ and $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has no zero in $(0,\delta)$, and extended uniquely to $(0,\infty)$ by the regular initial-value equation, and every solution that is not a multiple of $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has $|u(r)|/r$ unbounded as $r\downarrow0$;

(d) *termination.* $v$ is a polynomial if and only if $j\in\mathbb N_0$; in that case $v$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $L_j^{(2l+1)}$, and
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_j^{(2l+1)}(2kr)\quad(c\ne0)$$
lies in $L^2(0,\infty;dr)$;

(e) *eigenfunction.* If $j\in\mathbb N_0$ then $u_{\mathrm{reg}}\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu_{\mathrm{reg}}=-k^2u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; equivalently, for every $m$ the transported function $\psi(r\Omega):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap D(C)$ and satisfies $C\psi=-k^2\psi$.

The assertions are statements about the ordinary differential equation and
the operators $A_l,C$; no physical interpretation of $\gamma,k$ or of any
spectral level is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, and for
every $l\ge0$ let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]]; let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] (c),
with essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$
([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-essential-spectrum]]), and let $U$ be the polar unitary of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] (d). Then:

(a) if $k>0$ and $j:=\gamma/(2k)-l-1\notin\mathbb N_0$, then the regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] is not square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$, and $-k^2$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$;

(b) the negative eigenvalues of $A_l$ are exactly the numbers
$$-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2},\qquad n\ge l+1,$$
each with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the corresponding regular solution $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; in particular every negative eigenvalue of $A_l$ is simple;

(c) the negative eigenvalues of $C$ are exactly the numbers $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ with $n\ge1$;

(d) every eigenfunction of $C$ with negative eigenvalue lies in the closed span of the transported regular solutions: if $C\psi=E\psi$ with $E<0$ and $U\psi=(u_{lm})$, then $E=-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ for some $n\ge1$, and each nonzero $u_{lm}$ is a scalar multiple of the regular solution of $A_l$ at that energy.

This exhausts the negative spectrum of $A_l$ and of $C$ by the terminating
Laguerre solutions; no claim is made here about completeness of these
eigenfunctions in the negative spectral subspace, about the multiplicity of
the levels of $C$, or about any physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$ and let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be the
self-adjoint operator of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-infinitesimal-kinetic-bound]] with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$. For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$ and
$-l\le m\le l$ let $u_{nl}$ be the regular solution of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] at $k=\gamma/(2n)$
(the polynomial-exponential solution, unique up to a nonzero scalar), and put
$$\psi_{nlm}(x):=\frac{u_{nl}(r)}{r}Y_{lm}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega).$$
Then:

(a) each $\psi_{nlm}$ lies in $D(C)$ and $C\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\psi_{nlm}$; the vectors $\psi_{nlm}$ with distinct labels are pairwise orthogonal, and for fixed $n$ the eigenspace of $C$ at $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ is exactly their span; it has dimension $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^2$;

(b) after normalization, the family $(\psi_{nlm}/\|u_{nl}\|_2)_{n\ge1,0\le l\le n-1,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal family of the negative spectral subspace $E_C((-\infty,0))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$;

(c) the family is not complete in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$: the nonnegative spectral subspace $E_C([0,\infty))L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is nonzero (indeed infinite dimensional), so the bound states alone do not span $L^2$.

All claims concern the mathematical spectral decomposition of $C$; no physical
interpretation is asserted.

items.title: Ground radial probability and units

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 10.4 pp. 229-235 (lowest Coulomb eigenvalue, simplicity and ground-state formula; angular normalization is proved locally)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics (Cappella Archive), Section 8.1 pp. 186-193 (radial wavefunctions and radial probability densities of hydrogen, and the expectation values for powers of r)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(C)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above,
and put $a_0:=2/\gamma>0$. Define
$$\psi_{100}(x):=\Bigl(\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}\Bigr)^{1/2}e^{-r/a_0}\quad(x=r\Omega,\ r=|x|).$$
Then:

(a) $\psi_{100}\in D(C)$, $\|\psi_{100}\|_{L^2}=1$, and $C\psi_{100}=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4}\psi_{100}$;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, writing $dx$ for Lebesgue measure,
$$\int_B|\psi_{100}(x)|^2dx=\int_0^\infty\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}r^2e^{-2r/a_0}\Bigl(\int_{S^2}\mathbf1_B(r\Omega)d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr,$$
so the radial probability density $p(r):=\frac{\gamma^3}{2}r^2e^{-2r/a_0}=4r^2a_0^{-3}e^{-2r/a_0}$ is a probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p\ge0$ and $\int_0^\infty p(r)dr=1$;

(c) the mean of $p$ is $\int_0^\infty r\,p(r)dr=3a_0/2$, and the unique maximum (mode) of $p$ is at $r=a_0$;

(d) the spatial density $|\psi_{100}(x)|^2=\frac{\gamma^3}{8\pi}e^{-2r/a_0}$ is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at $x=0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a remainder $R_\varepsilon$ such that
$$
\int_{|x|<\varepsilon}|\psi_{100}(x)|^2\,dx=\frac16\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_0}\Bigr)^3+R_\varepsilon, \qquad |R_\varepsilon|\le\frac18\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_0}\Bigr)^4.
$$
Thus this probability is positive and tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and the spatial probability measure has no point atoms, including at the density maximum $x=0$;

(e) *parametrisation and dimensions.* If $\hbar,m,\kappa>0$ and $\gamma:=2m\kappa/\hbar^2$, then $a_0=\hbar^2/(m\kappa)$ and the operator
$$
C_{\hbar,m,\kappa}:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta-\frac{\kappa}{|\cdot|},\qquad D(C_{\hbar,m,\kappa})=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C),
$$
has eigenvalues $-\frac{m\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2n^2}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Bigl(-\frac{\gamma^2}{4n^2}\Bigr)$ ($n\ge1$); under the dimensional conventions $[\hbar]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[m]=\mathrm{kg}$, $[\kappa]=\mathrm{J\,m}$, the constants $a_0^2$ and $m\kappa^2/(2\hbar^2)$ have the dimensions of $\mathrm m^2$ and $\mathrm J$ respectively.

Clauses (a)–(d) are mathematical statements about the normalised ground vector
and its distribution; clause (e) is a dimensional-consistency statement about
the parametrisation and is not a physical claim, measurement or identification
of any quantity with nature.

items.title: Positive scaling of a self-adjoint operator: the spectral projection-valued measure transforms by the preimage of the scaling map
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a densely defined
self-adjoint operator with spectral projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel
$\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $c>0$. Write $cA$ for the operator
with $D(cA):=D(A)$ and $(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$, and for $m_{c}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
$m_{c}(\lambda):=c\lambda$, define
$$F(B):=E\bigl(m_{c}^{-1}(B)\bigr)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
Then:

(a) $F$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$;

(b) for every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ the bounded integrals
satisfy $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f\circ m_{c})$, and the operator
$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)$ of the spectral theorem equals $cA$ with
domain $D(A)$;

(c) consequently $F$ is the spectral projection valued measure $E_{cA}$ of
$cA$: for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{cA}(B)=E\bigl(c^{-1}B\bigr);$$in particular the negative spectral subspaces agree,$$E_{cA}\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H=E\bigl((-\infty,0)\bigr)H .$$

The assertion transfers the spectral measure along positive scaling of the
operator. It asserts no spectral type of a particular operator, no multiplicity
statement and no physical interpretation; $c<0$ is not covered, and no
statement is made about unbounded Borel functions of $cA$ beyond the identity
functional calculus stated in (b).

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m_1,m_2>0$, put
$M:=m_1+m_2$, $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$, let $\kappa>0$, $\hbar>0$, and define the
linear coordinate map
$$\Phi:\mathbb R^6\to\mathbb R^6,\qquad \Phi(x_1,x_2):=\Bigl(R,r\Bigr),\qquad R:=\frac{m_1x_1+m_2x_2}{M},\quad r:=x_1-x_2,$$
with inverse $x_1=R+\frac{m_2}{M}r$, $x_2=R-\frac{m_1}{M}r$. Write $L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ and for $f\in L^2$ put $(U_\Phi f)(R,r):=f(x_1,x_2)$ with $x_i$ expressed through $(R,r)$. Then:

(a) $\Phi$ is a linear isomorphism with $|\det\Phi|=1$, and $U_\Phi$ is a unitary operator on $L^2$;

(b) for every Schwartz function $f$, $U_\Phi(-(\hbar^2/2m_1)\Delta_{x_1}-(\hbar^2/2m_2)\Delta_{x_2})U_\Phi^{-1}f=(-(\hbar^2/2M)\Delta_R-(\hbar^2/2\mu)\Delta_r)f$; moreover both sides define the same self-adjoint operator on the common domain $H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$;

(c) the operator $H_2:=-(\hbar^2/2m_1)\Delta_{x_1}-(\hbar^2/2m_2)\Delta_{x_2}-\kappa/|x_1-x_2|$ with $D(H_2):=H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ is self-adjoint, and $U_\Phi H_2U_\Phi^{-1}=T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu$ under the identification $L^2(\mathbb R^6)\cong L^2(\mathbb R^3_R)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3_r)$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], where $T_R:=-(\hbar^2/2M)\Delta_R$ and $C_\mu:=-(\hbar^2/2\mu)\Delta_r-\kappa/|\cdot|$;

(d) $\sigma(H_2)=[-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2},\infty)$, and $H_2$ has no eigenvalues at all: the negative part of its spectrum is the interval $[-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2},0)$, consisting entirely of continuous spectrum, and each relative bound-state energy $-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2n^2}$ of $C_\mu$ is a threshold of the continuous spectrum of $H_2$ rather than an eigenvalue; in particular a relative bound state tensored with any centre-of-mass state is not an eigenvector of $H_2$;

(e) On $L^2(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C)$ define the centre-of-mass momentum component
$$
P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}:=\frac{\hbar}{i}\partial_{R_j},\qquad D(P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}):=\{g\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}g\in L^2\text{ as a weak derivative}\}.
$$
On the full two-body space define its lift
$$
\widetilde P_{R,j}:=U_\Phi^{-1}(P^{\mathrm{cm}}_{R,j}\otimes I)U_\Phi,\qquad D(\widetilde P_{R,j}):=U_\Phi^{-1}\{F\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R\times\mathbb R^3_r;\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}F\in L^2\text{ as a weak derivative}\}.
$$
Each $\widetilde P_{R,j}$ is self-adjoint and has no nonzero eigenvectors in $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$; hence there is no normalisable state of definite total momentum (a simultaneous eigenvector of the three lifted components).

All statements are mathematical statements about the operators on $L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ and the coordinate map; no physical interpretation, no identification of $m_1,m_2,\kappa,\hbar$ with measured constants, and no claim about nature is made.

$$Q_i\psi:=(\xi\mapsto\xi_i\,\psi(\xi)),\qquad D(Q_i):=\{\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C):\xi_i\psi\in L^2\}.$$

(a) each $Q_i$ is self-adjoint on $D(Q_i)$, the domain is a proper dense subspace of $L^2$, and every bound state satisfies $\psi_{nlm}\in D(Q_i)$, with $\|Q_i\psi_{nlm}\|_2^2=\int_0^\infty r^2|u_{nl}(r)|^2dr\cdot\int_{S^2}|\Omega_iY_{lm}(\Omega)|^2d\sigma(\Omega)<\infty$;

$$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle=\Bigl(\int_0^\infty r\,u_{n'l'}(r)\overline{u_{nl}(r)}\,dr\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_{S^2}Y_{l'm'}(\Omega)\overline{Q_q(\Omega)\,Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr),$$

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, $l\ge0$,
and let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] with form domain
$V_l$. Fix $k_{\min}>0$ and let $K:=\{k\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Re}k\ge k_{\min},\ \operatorname{Im}k\ge0\}$.
Then:

(a) *regular solution.* With $c_0:=1$, $c_{-1}:=0$ and
$$c_n:=-\frac{\gamma c_{n-1}+k^2c_{n-2}}{n(n+2l+1)}\qquad(n\ge1),$$
the series $\varphi_l(k,r):=r^{l+1}\sum_{n\ge0}c_nr^n$ converges for every $r>0$ and every $k\in\mathbb C$, the function $(k,r)\mapsto\varphi_l(k,r)$ is holomorphic in $k$ and $C^\infty$ in $r>0$, and $\varphi_l$ solves $-u''+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)u=k^2u$ with $\varphi_l(k,r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$;

(b) *Jost-type solution.* Put $a:=\gamma/(2k)$, $\theta(r):=kr+a\log r$, $w(r):=e^{i\theta(r)}$, $b:=a^2+l(l+1)+ia$ and consider the integral equation
$$v(r)=1+\int_r^\infty\frac{b}{s^2}\,w(s)^2\Bigl(\int_r^sw(y)^{-2}dy\Bigr)v(s)\,ds .$$
For every $k\in K$ with $k\ne0$ the equation has exactly one bounded solution $v(\cdot;k)$ on $[r_0,\infty)$ for some $r_0>0$ depending on $k$, and $v(r)=1+O(1/r)$, $v'(r)=O(1/r)$; the functions $f_l(k,r):=w(r)v(r)$ and $v$ are continuous on $K$, holomorphic in $k$ for $\operatorname{Im}k>0$, satisfy the radial equation $-\partial_r^2f_l+\bigl(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r\bigr)f_l=k^2f_l$ exactly, and obey the asymptotics
$$f_l=e^{i(kr+a\log r)}(1+O(1/r)),\qquad f_l'=e^{i(kr+a\log r)}[ik+O(1/r)]\qquad(r\to\infty);$$

(c) *Wronskians.* For real $k>0$ one has $W(\overline{f_l},f_l)=2ik$ and $W_l(k):=W(\varphi_l,f_l)\ne0$; consequently every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $Af_l+B\overline{f_l}$ with $A,B\in\mathbb C$, and $\varphi_l$ is a nonzero complex multiple combination of $f_l,\overline{f_l}$;

(d) *no positive eigenvalue.* For real $k>0$ and $A,B\in\mathbb C$, if $g=Af_l+B\overline{f_l}$ then $\int_R^L|g(r)|^2dr=(|A|^2+|B|^2)[L-R-\gamma\log(L/R)/(2k^2)]+O(1)$ as $L\to\infty$ with $R>r_0$ fixed; hence $g\in L^2(r_0,\infty)$ if and only if $A=B=0$, and $k^2>0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$.

All assertions concern the ordinary differential equation and the operator
$A_l$; no scattering amplitude, cross-section or physical interpretation is
asserted or computed.

items.title: Coulomb continuum spectral density

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 9.6 pp. 209-214 (spectral transformations II: boundary values of the Weyl-Titchmarsh m-function and the absolutely continuous spectrum) and Section 3.2 pp. 99-104 (Borel measures and the spectral measure of a self-adjoint operator)
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §13.7 (asymptotic expansions of Kummer solutions for large argument)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, $l\ge0$,
let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] with spectral
measure $E_{A_l}$, and for $k>0$ let $\varphi_l(k,\cdot)$ and $f_l(k,\cdot)$
be the solutions of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-jost-volterra-solution]], with
$W_l(k):=W(\varphi_l(k,\cdot),f_l(k,\cdot))\ne0$. Write
$$\rho_l(E):=\frac{\sqrt E}{\pi\,|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2}\qquad(E>0).$$

For $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ write $\mu_g(B):=\langle E_{A_l}(B)g,g\rangle$
for its finite positive scalar spectral measure, where $B\subseteq\mathbb R$
is Borel ([[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). A finite
positive Borel measure $\mu$ is *absolutely continuous* with respect to
Lebesgue measure $dE$ if $\mu(N)=0$ for every Borel set $N$ of Lebesgue measure
zero; it is *singular continuous* if it is carried by a Borel Lebesgue-null
set and has no atoms, meaning $\mu(\{E\})=0$ for every $E\in\mathbb R$.
Define the absolutely continuous subspace
$$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A_l):=\{g\in L^2(0,\infty):\mu_g\text{ is absolutely continuous with respect to }dE\}.$$
It is a closed linear subspace because it equals
$\bigcap_{N:\,|N|=0}\ker E_{A_l}(N)$, where the intersection is over Borel
Lebesgue-null sets and $\mu_g(N)=\|E_{A_l}(N)g\|^2$.
For $I=(0,\infty)$, put
$$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I):=\{g\in E_{A_l}(I)L^2(0,\infty):\mu_g\text{ is singular continuous}\}.$$
The set $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I)$ is a closed linear subspace:
linear combinations of such vectors have scalar measures supported on the
union of their null carriers and have no atoms, and these two properties pass
to limits of vectors by continuity of the PVM projections. Here $E_{A_l}(I)L^2$ is
*purely absolutely continuous* when it is contained in $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A_l)$,
and “$A_l$ has no singular-continuous spectrum on $I$” means
$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_l;I)=\{0\}$. Thus each operator spectral-type
phrase in (d) is a statement about the scalar PVM measures, not an additional
pointwise classification of energies.

Then:

(a) *resolvent kernel.* For $z=k^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}k>0$ and $k$ in the domain of the Jost construction, and for every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ with compact support, the resolvent is given by
$$((A_l-z)^{-1}g)(r)=\int_0^\infty G_l(r,s)g(s)\,ds,\qquad G_l(r,s):=-\frac{\varphi_l(k,\min(r,s))\,f_l(k,\max(r,s))}{W_l(k)},$$
and $G_l$ solves $(A_l-z)G_l=\delta$ in the sense that $-G''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)G-zG=0$ away from $r=s$ and the derivative of $G$ has the jump $-1$ at $r=s$; moreover $\|(A_l-z)^{-1}\|\le1/|\operatorname{Im}z|$;

(b) *boundary value.* For real $k>0$ one has $\varphi_l(k,\cdot)$ real and, for all $r,s>0$,
$$\operatorname{Im}G_l(k^2+i0;r,s)=\frac{k\,\varphi_l(k,r)\varphi_l(k,s)}{|W_l(k)|^2};$$

(c) *spectral density.* For every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ and every $0<a<b$,
$$\langle E_{A_l}((a,b))g,g\rangle=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\frac1\pi\int_a^b\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle(A_l-E-i\varepsilon)^{-1}g,g\bigr\rangle dE,$$
and if $g$ has compact support then
$$\langle E_{A_l}((a,b))g,g\rangle=\int_a^b\rho_l(E)\Bigl|\int_0^\infty\varphi_l(\sqrt E,r)g(r)\,dr\Bigr|^2dE;$$
consequently for compactly supported $g$ the measure $E_{A_l,g}(B):=\langle E_{A_l}(B)g,g\rangle$ restricted to $(0,\infty)$ is absolutely continuous with density $\rho_l(E)|\int\varphi_l g|^2$;

(d) *absolutely continuous spectrum; no zero eigenvalue.* For every $g\in L^2(0,\infty)$ the measure $E_{A_l,g}$ has no atom in $(0,\infty)$; the positive spectral subspace $E_{A_l}((0,\infty))L^2(0,\infty)$ is purely absolutely continuous and is the closed span of the positive spectral projections of compactly supported functions; it equals the absolutely continuous subspace of $A_l$, and $A_l$ has no singular continuous spectrum on $(0,\infty)$; moreover $0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_l$.

No scattering phase, normalization of the continuum functions as a unitary
transform, or physical cross-section is asserted; the transform itself is the
subject of the companion item [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-onto-radial-continuum-transform]].

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma\ge0$, $l\ge0$,
let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] with spectral
measure $E_{A_l}$ and form domain $V_l$, and for $E>0$ let
$\varphi_l(\sqrt E,\cdot)$ and $\rho_l(E)=\frac{\sqrt E}{\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2}$
be as in [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-continuum-spectral-density]]. Define, for $g$ in
the dense subspace $C_c$ of compactly supported square-integrable functions,
$$(T_lg)(E):=\sqrt{\rho_l(E)}\int_0^\infty\varphi_l(\sqrt E,r)g(r)\,dr\qquad(E>0).$$
Then:

(a) $T_lg\in L^2((0,\infty),dE)$ and $\|T_lg\|^2=\langle E_{A_l}((0,\infty))g,g\rangle$; consequently $T_l$ extends uniquely to a linear contraction $T:H\to L^2((0,\infty),dE)$, where $H:=L^2((0,\infty),dr)$ and $P_+:=E_{A_l}((0,\infty))$, with $\|Tg\|=\|P_+g\|$ for every $g\in H$. Its restriction is a linear isometry
$$\widehat T_l:E_{A_l}((0,\infty))L^2(0,\infty)\longrightarrow L^2((0,\infty),dE)$$
of the positive spectral subspace of $A_l$ into $L^2((0,\infty),dE)$, satisfying $T=\widehat T_lP_+$ and $T_lg=\widehat T_l(P_+g)$ for $g\in C_c$. Equivalently, $P_+g\mapsto T_lg$ is a well-defined isometry on the dense projected core $P_+C_c\subseteq P_+H$ and $\widehat T_l$ is its unique isometric extension;

(b) $\widehat T_l$ is onto, hence unitary; equivalently the range of $\widehat T_l$ is all of $L^2((0,\infty),dE)$ and the adjoint $\widehat T_l^*$ is an isometry inverse to $\widehat T_l$;

(c) $\widehat T_lA_l\widehat T_l^*$ is multiplication by the independent variable on the domain $\{h\in L^2((0,\infty),dE):\int E^2|h(E)|^2dE<\infty\}$, and $\widehat T_lh(A_l)\widehat T_l^*$ is multiplication by $h$ for every bounded Borel function $h$;

(d) *complete Coulomb spectral resolution.* If $\gamma>0$, the operator $C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ is unitarily equivalent to the diagonal operator
$$\bigoplus_{(l,m)}\Bigl[\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\ge l+1}\mathbb C\Bigr)\oplus L^2((0,\infty),dE)\Bigr]$$
with the constant $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ on the $(n,l,m)$-copy of $\mathbb C$ and multiplication by $E$ on each continuum copy; equivalently there is a unitary $V$ from $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ onto the displayed direct sum with $VCV^*$ equal to that diagonal operator, and the negative part of the spectrum is exhausted by the bound states of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] while the positive part is purely absolutely continuous. If $\gamma=0$, the representation is $\bigoplus_{(l,m)}L^2((0,\infty),dE)$ with multiplication by $E$ and no discrete copies, because the free Fourier multiplier has no nonpositive spectral projection.

The transform is a mathematical spectral representation of $A_l$ and $C$; no
scattering amplitude, phase shift or physical interpretation is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above, and
fix $g\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\mathbb C)$ with
$$\int_0^\infty\varphi_0(1,r)g(r)\,dr=1,$$
where $\varphi_0(1,\cdot)$ is the regular solution of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-jost-volterra-solution]] at $k=1$, $l=0$. Such a $g$ exists
because $\varphi_0(1,\cdot)$ is nonzero and locally square-integrable. Put
$$\psi(x):=\frac{g(r)}{r}Y_{00}(\Omega)\qquad(x=r\Omega).$$
This example verifies concretely that:

(a) $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and the coefficients of $\psi$ in the polar decomposition of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] vanish except in the $(0,0)$-block, where they equal $g$;

(b) $\langle E_C((0,\infty))\psi,\psi\rangle=\int_0^\infty\rho_0(E)\bigl|\int_0^\infty\varphi_0(\sqrt E,r)g(r)dr\bigr|^2dE>0$;

(c) consequently the closed span of the bound states $(\psi_{nlm})$ of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] is a proper subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$: the bound states alone are not a complete eigenbasis, and the nonnegative continuous spectral projection is indispensable.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m_1,m_2,\mu,M,\kappa,\hbar$
be as in [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]], let $C_\mu$ and $T_R$ be
the relative and centre-of-mass kinetic operators there, let
$u_1\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_r)$ be any nonzero relative ground vector with
$C_\mu u_1=E_1u_1$, where $E_1=-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2}$, and let
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C)$ be a nonzero centre-of-mass
test function. Consider the product vector
$$\Psi:=\varphi\otimes u_1\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3_r),$$
viewed as an element of $L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ through the identification of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. This example verifies
that:

(a) $(T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu)\Psi=E_1\Psi+(T_R\varphi)\otimes u_1$, and $T_R\varphi\ne0$, so $\Psi$ is not an eigenvector of the two-body operator;

(b) $\langle(T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\|u_1\|^2(E_1\|\varphi\|^2+\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle)>E_1\|\Psi\|^2$: the product vector has energy strictly above the bottom $E_1$ of the two-body spectrum, and the bottom is not attained. When $\|u_1\|=1$, the identity reduces to $E_1\|\varphi\|^2+\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle$;

(c) the relative bound state $u_1$ is an eigenvector of the relative operator $C_\mu$, but the two-body operator has no eigenvalues at all ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] (d)); the relative bound energy is a threshold of the continuous spectrum of the total operator, so "relative bound state" and "bound state of the two-body problem" are distinct notions.
